the TypeScript base configuration every package extends

inputs.reason: Every CLI command a CLI test starts reads the parsed repository configuration; the selector forces the CLI suite on its change for the same reason.
The lockfile decides every installed dependency every suite runs against; it is read as its dependency identity, so a workspace folder or local path move alone changes no installed dependency.
The test starts the probe as its own process, outside any import.
The loader test validates every process folder against the contract schema it reads from disk.
The golden comparison reads the snapshot's bytes from disk.
The inventory test reads real lockfiles from before and after two workspace moves from disk, outside any import.
The pr command test reads this pull-request body fixture from disk, outside any import.
Each reads the workflow file from disk and asserts its jobs and steps.
The compatibility suite packs the command-line bundle and doctrine and installs its tarball.
The compatibility suite starts the command-line package's build and doctrine copy as their own processes before packing it.
The compatibility suite reads the fixed release group that names the published packages, and the snapshot it compares their facts with, from disk.
Each reads the advisory macOS sandbox workflow from disk and asserts its job and steps.
The CI plan's hand-written replay table and its pinned base commit, read from disk by the job oracle and the plan's own test.
Both tests load the CI plan's scripts by path at run time, outside the CLI's type program, so no import edge reaches them.
The job oracle derives each package's typecheck prerequisites from turbo's own dry-run task graph.
The shard lists place each CLI test in a shard; the schedule reads them to place every other shard-run test.
The native local runner's test reads the committed hook and asserts where it hands a push's tests to the adapter.
The inventory check's test validates the committed declarations against the tree; the schedule tests place the tests they declare.
The runtime regression executes the GC and synchronous-child probe in an asynchronously supervised process.
The selection library's committed fixture repositories, read from disk by its own tests and by the repository-side library test.
The forge-write and pull-request report tests moved into the process with their code; they read the CLI's forge body fixtures from disk and start its fake body checks as programs, outside any import.
The header parity test compares the parsed event headers its probes write with this recording, read from disk.

Each test writes a program that imports the Log client or the process's sink factory and branch reader by path and starts it with bun, outside any import; the factory folder and the client are named whole, and what they import in turn reaches these tests only through their own imports, the conservative reading.
The dispatch child-process test replays the CLI's recorded Codex stream through the dispatch role log, read from disk.
The dispatch helpers test reads two credential-shaped test files verbatim, so the after-turn credential scan is proven against the bytes the repository ships.
The configuration golden parses its corpus and its recorded snapshot from disk and compares the composed schema's answers against them, outside any import.

The configuration golden lists every tracked vinaya.config*.json with git ls-files and parses each from disk. These are the files that scan finds today. The `git ls-files` call also makes the selector read the test as a whole-tree scanner, the conservative fallback that selects it on any change: a newly tracked configuration file anywhere fails the golden until its snapshot is rewritten.
Conservative tree-scan roots: the placement test checks every old file is absent under these folders, so additions anywhere in them must select the guard.
The placement guard reads source-comment roots and checks the exact moved-file set.
Conservative folder edge for the moved parsers that read core fixtures with filesystem paths, retaining all fixture-triggered coverage.
Conservative folder edge for moved forge-reader tests and the Issue opener that load captured Issue bodies and milestone JSON outside imports.
The symbol-collision test preserves its pre-move source census and logical identities while reading relocated implementations at their destinations.
The navigation test reads doctrine pages and their enforcement anchors from disk.

The doctrine resolution, the doctrine map's readers, the AGENTS.md pointer, the Log's doctrine version, the retired-role sweep, the action and diagram-model cross-checks, the node routes, the doctrine command's tests and the bundler's test read the doctrine files at the source paths the doctrine map names, so a moved or renamed doctrine file selects them even when its text is unchanged.
The doctrine-shape test reads the developer role and its reference through the resolved doctrine root.
The runner-default test reads the repository configuration from disk.

providers.reason: The sandbox suite skips itself unless a pull request changes one of these paths, so each is an input of that suite.
Each folder-scanning test reads the roots it declares from disk.

policies.duty: the tests this list names run on every push, whatever changed
a push to the default branch runs every suite's every test
the atta-labs/secret-scan check scans the whole tree on every change
the bundler oracle in harness/processes/vinaya-strict/integration/test-selector-oracle.test.ts runs when the selection logic, its inputs or the inventory change, and on every default-branch run
the build job checks the inventory and runs the repository suite on every pull request, documentation-only ones included
the build job runs the package-compatibility suite on every pull request, documentation-only ones included, whatever the change selects
